title: Completed compact-support exchange map
statement:
Let
$$\begin{array}{ccc}X'&\xrightarrow{g'}&X\\ f'\downarrow&&\downarrow f\\ Y'&\xrightarrow{g}&Y\end{array}$$
be a compact-support square [def-cbc-compact-support-square]. Choose a compactification $c=(j,p)$, $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}Y$, and its base change $c'=(j',p')$, with $\bar g':\overline X'=\overline X\times_Y Y'\to\overline X$. The open immersions $j,j'$ are quasi-compact: apply [lemma-nagata-open-immersion-qc-over-separated-target] to $X\to\overline X\to Y$ and $X'\to\overline X'\to Y'$; the structural map $f$ is of finite type by [def-cbc-compact-support-square], and its base change $f'$ is of finite type by [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change]; the maps $p,p'$ are separated because they are proper. Use the adic datum and completed coefficient sheaves of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. All categories $D(W_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ below are $D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_W))$, not categories for discrete non-torsion constant coefficients. Ordinary module derived pullback, direct image and adjunctions are [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], using the canonical coefficient identifications [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image].

For $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ derived $I$-complete [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion], form $M=j_!K$ using the localized ringed-site extension by zero [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]. Its coefficient sheaf is $A_{\overline X}|_X=A_X$, since slice restriction commutes objectwise with limits [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization]. It is applied termwise to complexes by [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. The complex $M$ is complete by [lem-cbc-completed-extension-zero-comparison], applied to the identity base-change square of the quasi-compact open $j$, and $Rp_*M$ is complete by [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits]. For each of these complete objects $C$, [prop-weil-pbc-koszul-reconstruction] gives the natural isomorphism $c_C:C^{\wedge}_{\mathrm{Kos}}\xrightarrow{\sim}R\lim C_\bullet$ with $c_C\eta_C=\operatorname{comp}_C$. Thus its canonical quotient-tower map $\operatorname{comp}_C$ is an isomorphism, exactly the completeness hypothesis in [def-weil-pbc-completed-base-change-map] and [lem-weil-pbc-strict-tower-exchange-mate-normalization]; this uses the specified unit, rather than an arbitrary isomorphism to a limit. In the compactification-relative notation [def-weil-pbc-projection-compactification] put
$$Rf_!^cK=Rp_*j_!K,\qquad Rf'_!^{c'}L=Rp'_*j'_!L.$$

Construct the proper completed factor in the derived category of strict towers, as follows. This specifies the same strict lift used by proper base change when its etale-origin hypotheses hold. Write $J=\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}}$, $\Delta$ for the constant $J$-diagram, and $Q_{T,\bullet}=((P_n)_T)_n$ with the quotient transitions. Use the small ringed diagram sites of [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization], with ring sheaf $\Delta A_T$, and put
$$\mathcal R_T(F)=\Delta F\otimes^L_{\Delta A_T}Q_{T,\bullet}.$$
This is the strict reduction functor of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], with the finite-level modules restricted to $A_T$-modules. In particular its value is an object of $D(\operatorname{Tow}_A(T))$, not just a sequence in $D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_T))$. Write $\mathscr L_u$ for the derived termwise pullback of [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] and $\mathscr P_u=Ru_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}$ for the derived termwise direct image of [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits]. The canonical pullback/reduction tensor identifications give strict natural isomorphisms
$$t_{u,F}:\mathcal R_U(Lu^*F)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathscr L_u\mathcal R_V(F)\qquad(u:U\to V).$$
Use the coefficient identifications of [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image] and the derived tensor comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. These are comparisons on the diagram sites. A diagonal flat-term K-flat representative of $F$ is K-flat there: its tensor with an acyclic diagram is acyclic at each index, hence acyclic by [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. On these representatives the level-$n$ comparison is the balancing isomorphism $(u^*QF)\otimes_{A_U}(P_n)_U\cong u_n^*(QF\otimes_{A_V}(P_n)_V)$. For the transition $P_{n+1}\to P_n$, both composites send the pulled-back $q$ tensored with $p$ to the pulled-back $q$ tensored with the quotient image of $p$. Thus the comparisons respect the specified strict transitions.

For $F\in D(U_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ define a strict projection map
$$\Pi_{u,F}:\mathcal R_V(Ru_*F)\longrightarrow\mathscr P_u\mathcal R_U(F)$$
by the projection-formula adjunct of counit tensored with identity, on these diagram sites with coefficient object $Q_{V,\bullet}$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] [def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-map]. Its source uses the canonical identification $\mathscr P_u\Delta F=\Delta Ru_*F$. To fix that identification, compute both sides using $\Delta I_F$, for a K-injective representative $I_F$ of $F$: $\Delta$ is right adjoint to the exact evaluation at the terminal index $1$ of $J$, so preserves K-injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective]; underived direct image on diagrams is termwise. Thus this source identification uses the identity of the corresponding direct-image complexes. Evaluation at $n$ also preserves K-injectives: its left adjoint sends a module $V$ to the diagram equal to $V$ at indices $m\leq n$ and zero at $m>n$, with identity nonzero transition maps, and that left adjoint is exact. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective]. Evaluation preserves the K-flat representatives and tensor comparison by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. The fraction characterization of the canonical derived adjunction in [lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general] therefore identifies evaluation of the diagram counit-tensor adjunct with the ordinary counit-tensor adjunct: the termwise adjunction transposes each component and the same representative complexes compute both localized adjunctions. Thus evaluation of $\Pi_{u,F}$ is the ordinary projection-formula map with $(P_n)_V$, hence is invertible by [lemma-weil-pbc-perfect-projection-formula]. The cone of $\Pi_{u,F}$ has acyclic evaluations; kernels, cokernels, and therefore cohomology of tower complexes are levelwise [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian], so $\Pi_{u,F}$ is invertible in the derived strict-tower category. This does not assume that $Q_{V,\bullet}$ is perfect as one diagram-site object, or that evaluations are faithful on morphisms.

For the proper square $(p,p',g,\bar g')$ let
$$e_M:Lg^*Rp_*M\longrightarrow Rp'_*L\bar g'^*M$$
be the specified ambient ringed mate of [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange]. Put $N=Lg^*Rp_*M$, $E=L\bar g'^*M$, $F=Rp'_*E$, and define the strict corners and comparison maps
$$\begin{aligned}
 A_\bullet&=\mathscr L_g\mathcal R_Y(Rp_*M),&
 B_\bullet&=\mathscr L_g\mathscr P_p\mathcal R_{\overline X}(M),&
 D_\bullet&=\mathscr P_{p'}\mathscr L_{\bar g'}\mathcal R_{\overline X}(M),\\
 H&=(\mathscr L_g\Pi_{p,M})\circ t_{g,Rp_*M}:\mathcal R_{Y'}(N)\xrightarrow{\sim}B_\bullet,\\
 H'&=(\mathscr P_{p'}t_{\bar g',M})\circ\Pi_{p',E}:\mathcal R_{Y'}(F)\xrightarrow{\sim}D_\bullet,\\
 v_\bullet&=H'\circ\mathcal R_{Y'}(e_M)\circ H^{-1}:B_\bullet\longrightarrow D_\bullet.
\end{aligned}$$
In particular $v_\bullet$ is a specified morphism in $D(\operatorname{Tow}_A(Y'))$. No lift is selected from its individual evaluations.

Let $a:Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}Rp_*M\xrightarrow{\sim}R\lim A_\bullet$ be precisely the identification from [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback], and set
$$s=(R\lim(\mathscr L_g\Pi_{p,M}))\circ a:Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}Rp_*M\xrightarrow{\sim}R\lim B_\bullet.$$
For $T_\bullet=\mathscr L_{\bar g'}\mathcal R_{\overline X}(M)$ let
$$c_{p',T}:Rp'_*R\lim T_\bullet\xrightarrow{\sim}R\lim\mathscr P_{p'}T_\bullet=R\lim D_\bullet$$
be the specified direct-image/derived-limit comparison of [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits]. Define
$$\gamma_M=c_{p',T}^{-1}\circ R\lim(v_\bullet)\circ s:
Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}Rp_*M\longrightarrow Rp'_*L\bar g'^*_{\mathrm{comp}}M,$$
where $R\lim$ on strict towers is the triangulated functor of [prop-weil-pbc-rlim-functoriality]. This construction needs no etale-origin witnesses to define a morphism.

When the reductions $M_n$ carry the compatible etale-origin witnesses of [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness], this $\gamma_M$ is exactly $\operatorname{Ex}^{\mathrm{comp}}_{(p,p',g,\bar g'),M}$ of [def-weil-pbc-completed-base-change-map], the map used in [thm-weil-pbc-complete-proetale]. Indeed [lem-weil-pbc-strict-tower-exchange-mate-normalization] specifies that definition's strict lift by these same $H,H'$ and the equation $v'_\bullet=H'\mathcal R_{Y'}(e_M)H^{-1}$. Its $H$ is the pullback of the same diagram-site counit-tensor projection map, and its $H'$ is that map for $p',E$ followed by the same pullback/reduction comparison. Consequently $v_\bullet=v'_\bullet$ in the derived strict-tower category itself, $s$ is the specified $R\lim(h_\bullet)$ after $a$, and $c_{p',T}$ is the specified target comparison. The two ordered composites therefore have identical three factors. This identifies the morphisms, not only their source and target or their finite evaluations; the proper-base-change theorem can be applied to this factor whenever its stated witness hypotheses hold.

Let
$$\beta_K:L\bar g'^*_{\mathrm{comp}}j_!K\xrightarrow{\sim}j'_!Lg'^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K$$
be the canonical completed extension-by-zero comparison of [lem-cbc-completed-extension-zero-comparison], for the upper open square $(j,j',\bar g',g')$. Define the *completed compact-support exchange map* attached to $c,c'$ to be the ordered composite
$$\begin{aligned}\operatorname{Ex}^{\mathrm{comp},c}_!(K):\quad Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}Rf_!^cK&=Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}Rp_*j_!K\\&\xrightarrow{\gamma_{j_!K}}Rp'_*L\bar g'^*_{\mathrm{comp}}j_!K\\&\xrightarrow{Rp'_*(\beta_K)}Rp'_*j'_!Lg'^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K=Rf'_!^{c'}Lg'^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K.\end{aligned}$$
This is the completed-coefficient compactification formula, paralleling the finite etale formula [def-cbc-exchange-map]. It asserts neither compactification independence nor invertibility; those require separate theorems. In particular no etale-origin hypothesis or identification with condensed-module coefficients is implicit in this definition.

blueprint_update.statement:
In the situation of [def-cbc-exchange-map], let $(A,I)$
satisfy [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] and let
$K\in D(X_{\Proet},A)$ be derived $I$-complete. For a
compactification $c=(j,p)$ and its base change $c'$, define the
*completed compact-support exchange map*

$$
\Ex^{\mathrm{comp}}_!(K):
Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}Rf_!K\longrightarrow Rf'_!Lg'^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K
$$

as the composite of the completed proper-base-change exchange map of
[thm-weil-pbc-complete-proetale] applied to $p$ and
$j_!K$, with the completed extension-by-zero comparison
$Lg'^*_{\mathrm{comp}}j_!K\xrightarrow{\sim}j'_!Lg'^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K$
of [lem-cbc-completed-extension-zero-comparison].

lean.statement: def completedCompactSupportExchange {A : Type (t + 1)} [CommRing A] (d : AdicCoefficientDatum A) {X' X Y' Y : Scheme.{t}} {f : X ⟶ Y} {f' : X' ⟶ Y'} {g : Y' ⟶ Y} {g' : X' ⟶ X} [QuasiCompact f] (c : Compactification f) (c' : Compactification f') (gbar : c'.Z ⟶ c.Z) (properSquare : ChosenCartesianSquare gbar c'.g c.g g) (openSquare : OpenImmersionSquare g' c'.i c.i gbar) (r : ℕ) (a : Fin r → A) (ha : Ideal.span (Set.range a) = d.ideal) (K : (cbcCompleteProperty d X r a ha).FullSubcategory) : (d.completedPull g).obj ((d.push c.g).obj ((cbcDerivedOpenShriek d c.i c.isOpenImmersion).obj K.obj)) ⟶ (d.push c'.g).obj ((cbcDerivedOpenShriek d c'.i c'.isOpenImmersion).obj ((d.completedPull g').obj K.obj))
lean.note: The map is the specified ambient strict-tower completedExchange followed by direct image of cbcDatumCompletedExchange. Both factors use d.completedPull. Two supplied Cartesian squares express a chosen base-changed compactification, allowing any canonically identified presentation. A compactification supplies separatedness and local finite type; QuasiCompact f supplies the remaining finite-type condition. No etale-origin witnesses are required to define the map.
